question: What did Kestrel think of OrbitFlow's website?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract what the Kestrel Robotics representatives say about OrbitFlow's website, including its design, usability, navigation, content, performance, and any opinions, praise, or complaints about it.
assumptions: 'Kestrel' refers to Kestrel Robotics, the only catalogue company starting with Kestrel.
'Website' includes homepage, landing pages and web portal references.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: Your website. It's very enterprise. Governance, compliance, workspace separation. We're a hundred and fifty people building robots. I looked at it and thought, that's not for us.
findings.context: Rafael Santos said OrbitFlow's website looked very enterprise, with governance, compliance and workspace separation, which made him think it was not for Kestrel's size of company. — Stated reason he crossed OrbitFlow off the evaluation list; the complaint concerns the website's positioning/content, not usability or performance.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: That's a fair read of our website.
findings.context: Leo Grant (OrbitFlow) agreed that the website read as enterprise and explained it is aimed at companies with a governance function, which Kestrel lacks. — Vendor concedes the website's positioning is off-target for Kestrel, while claiming the product itself may still fit.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Our marketing is aimed at companies with a governance function. You don't have one, so it isn't aimed at you.
findings.context: OrbitFlow's own rep said the marketing is aimed at companies with a governance function, so the website is not aimed at Kestrel. — Vendor acknowledges the website targets a different buyer; separates marketing fit from product fit.

draft.answer: Kestrel Robotics' COO Rafael Santos thought OrbitFlow's website looked very enterprise and concluded the product was not for a 150-person company [C1]. OrbitFlow's Account Executive Leo Grant agreed it was a fair read and said the marketing targets companies with a governance function, which Kestrel lacks [C2].

claims.text: Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics) said OrbitFlow's website looked very enterprise, citing governance, compliance and workspace separation, and thought 'that's not for us' as a 150-person robot-building company. This was his stated reason for crossing OrbitFlow off the list; the complaint is about positioning/content, not usability or performance.

Leo Grant (OrbitFlow Account Executive) agreed it was 'a fair read' of the website and said OrbitFlow's marketing is aimed at companies with a governance function, which Kestrel doesn't have, so it isn't aimed at them.
